title: The Tragic Life of Vincent Van Gogh
summary: Josh and Chuck (credited in the transcript as the iHeart Intro speaker) discuss the life of Vincent van Gogh, from his early jobs in the art trade and failed preaching in Belgian coal country, through his Paris period, move to Arles and the Yellow House, the Gauguin fight and ear incident, his sanitarium stay at Saint-Rémy where he painted The Starry Night, his time at Auvers, his death in July 1890, and how sister-in-law Jo Bonger promoted his work posthumously. They also cover his suspected mental illness and epilepsy, a myth-busting note about his sales, and end with a listener email about the Boeing 737 MAX.
topics: Walt Whitman influence on Starry Night

segments.title: Opening banter and van Gogh films
segments.summary: Hosts joke around, then discuss van Gogh movies (Loving Vincent, Vincent & Theo) and a documentary they watched, and their appreciation for van Gogh's art.

segments.title: Early life, art trade, and failed preaching
segments.summary: Van Gogh's birth in 1853 in Zundert, boarding school, work at an uncle's art dealership until he was fired, then an unordained preacher in Belgian coal country until dismissed; his father's approval and his sympathy for workers.

segments.title: Turning to art and Theo's support
segments.summary: Van Gogh decides to become an artist, studies painting, and is supported financially by brother Theo and cousin Anton Mauve, who taught him oil and watercolor; hosts discuss the myth that he sold only one painting.
topics: van Gogh sold one painting myth

segments.title: Sien Hornik, The Potato Eaters, and early paintings
segments.summary: Van Gogh's relationship with Sien Hornik and family opposition, his peasant studies and The Potato Eaters, which was poorly received, and Still Life with Bible after his father's death in 1885.

segments.title: Move to Paris and productivity
segments.summary: Move to Paris near Theo, shift to brighter palette, and the hosts discuss his prolific output of nearly 900 paintings in about a decade and his pace across locations.

segments.title: Japanese influence, Arles, and Yellow House
segments.summary: Influence of Japanese woodblock prints (copy of Hiroshige), depression intensified in Paris, move to Arles in Provence in 1888, and the Yellow House and sunflower paintings.

segments.title: Viewing the paintings and Starry Night over the Rhône
segments.summary: Hosts discuss close-up viewing of van Gogh brushwork and his first Starry Night, Starry Night over the Rhône (1888), and how criticism affected him.

segments.title: Gauguin, the ear incident, and hospitalization
segments.summary: Gauguin's stay at the Yellow House, the Christmas Eve 1888 absinthe and razor confrontation, the ear cutting and brothel story with its alternate theories, hospital stay, epilepsy diagnosis and potassium bromide, and later checking into the Saint-Rémy sanitarium.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break; no sponsor read captured in the transcript.

segments.title: The Starry Night painting and Walt Whitman
segments.summary: Van Gogh paints The Starry Night while at the sanitarium, likely inspired by Walt Whitman's poetry, and it is now highly visited at MoMA in New York.

segments.title: Marriage of Theo, Almond Blossom, and final months
segments.summary: Theo marries Jo Bonger and names their son Vincent; van Gogh paints Almond Blossom for the baby. He submits to the Salon and gets first critical notice from Albert Aurier. Then he moves near Paris under a doctor's care, paints intensely, visits Theo, and Theo plans to open his own dealership.

segments.title: Death and posthumous reputation
segments.summary: Van Gogh shoots himself on July 27, 1890; Theo dies six months later. Jo Bonger inherits the paintings, studies the letters, and promotes his work, aided by critic Jan Veth; the Van Gogh Museum opened in 1973.

segments.title: Mental illness diagnoses and family history
segments.summary: Possible diagnoses including epilepsy, bipolar disorder and schizophrenia, alcohol use, and family history such as a sister with schizophrenia and brother Cornelius's death in South Africa.

segments.title: Cafe foreclosure and paintings auctioned
segments.summary: A Paris cafe exhibiting early van Gogh works was foreclosed; his paintings were auctioned in bundles of ten and sold as blank canvases.

segments.title: Listener mail: Boeing 737 MAX
segments.summary: A listener who is an embedded control software engineer writes about the 737 MAX failures and the single point of failure in its system, rating the episode ten out of ten.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listener email and close the show.
